bounded_statement: The selected result's inferential claim (Welch two-sample t-test over 30 strikes per material, t = 17.11, df = 40.2, p < 1e-15) is not supported as stated, because each of the 12 machine-tool bases — the declared independent unit (base_id) — contributes 5 repeated strike rows that are all entered into the row-independent two-sample t-test as separate observations. The effective number of independent units is 6 per material, not 30, so the reported degrees of freedom, t statistic, and p-value overstate the strength of evidence; this bounded statement concerns the validity of the reported test quantities, not the direction of the material effect, which may survive a correct base-level reanalysis.

counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow does read base_id (COL_UNIT) and correctly reports the number of distinct bases per material (6 each), showing the analyst was aware of the clustering structure; however, this information is used only for descriptive text, not to correct the inference.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: bases[material] used only for reporting counts

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the pseudoreplication finding in three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow aggregates to one value per base before testing (e.g., mean per base_id) or uses any cluster-aware method: read_strikes appends one value per row with no groupby, and base_id is stored only in a set used for counting, so no aggregation or correction exists. (2) I checked whether each base_id might in fact appear only once in the data, which would make strike-level and base-level analysis identical: the CSV shows exactly 5 rows per base_id (60 rows, 12 bases), and the report itself states 30 observations per material from 6 bases, so repetition is confirmed. (3) I checked whether the clustering could be inferentially harmless by inspecting the variance structure: within-base spread of damping_ratio_pct is roughly 0.05-0.08 percentage points while between-base spread within a material is roughly 0.5-1.1 percentage points, so strikes are strongly correlated within base and the effective sample size is close to the number of bases (6 per group), not 30. All three falsification routes failed to overturn the finding; the reported df = 40.2 and p < 1e-15 are artifacts of entering each independent unit five times. The only surviving mitigation is that the effect direction and magnitude appear robust at the base level, which I recorded as counterevidence and reflected in the bounded statement.

root_cause: The workflow's read_strikes function flattens the data by appending every strike's damping_ratio_pct into a single per-material list (workflow/analysis.py line 35), and main() passes these strike-level lists directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind (line 65) with no per-base aggregation, mixed/hierarchical model, or cluster-robust correction. base_id is read only to count bases for descriptive text (line 36), never to enforce one entry per independent unit, so each base enters the row-independent procedure five times, inflating n from 6 to 30 per group and shrinking the p-value and standard errors accordingly.
